name: public-docs-qa
description: Hand-written questions over the 5 public-domain documents in eval/corpus. Answerable items carry verbatim evidence spans (a retrieved chunk is relevant if it comes from docId and contains one span, whitespace/case-insensitive) and short gold answers (an answer is correct if it is not a refusal and contains one gold string, case-insensitive). Unanswerable items ask about things the corpus does not state; the correct behaviour is to refuse.

cases.question: How can the terms and conditions of the commercial contract be changed?
evidence: may be made only by written agreement of the parties

cases.question: Which FAR clause is used to resolve disputes under the commercial contract terms?
evidence: in accordance with the clause at Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.233-1, Disputes

cases.question: How many copies must accompany the original invoice submitted by the Contractor?
evidence: submit an original invoice and three copies

cases.question: When does risk of loss pass to the Government if transportation is f.o.b. origin?
evidence: Delivery of the supplies to a carrier, if transportation is f.o.b. origin

cases.question: Does the contract price include Federal, State, and local taxes?
evidence: The contract price includes all applicable Federal, State, and local taxes and duties
answers: includes all applicable federal, state, and local taxes

cases.question: If the Government terminates for convenience, how is the Contractor paid?
evidence: paid a percentage of the contract price reflecting the percentage of the work performed prior to the notice of termination

cases.question: What happens if the Government improperly terminated the contract for default?
evidence: improperly terminated this contract for default, such termination shall be deemed a termination for convenience

cases.question: When does title to items furnished under the contract pass to the Government?
evidence: title to items furnished under this contract shall pass to the Government upon acceptance

cases.question: Is the Contractor liable for consequential damages from defects in accepted items?
evidence: will not be liable to the Government for consequential damages
answers: not be liable to the government for consequential damages

cases.question: Under the time-and-materials alternate, when are services and materials presumed accepted?
evidence: presumed accepted 60 days after the date of delivery

cases.question: Under the time-and-materials alternate, what portion of the hourly rate is attributable to profit?
evidence: attributable to profit shall be 10 percent

cases.question: Amounts payable by the Contractor to the Government bear interest unless paid within how many days of becoming due?
evidence: unless paid within 30 days of becoming due

cases.question: What kinds of occurrences count as excusable delays for the Contractor?
evidence: acts of God or the public enemy

cases.question: Who must indemnify whom against patent, trademark or copyright infringement claims?
evidence: The Contractor shall indemnify the Government and its officers, employees and agents against liability

cases.question: Are indemnification clauses in an End User License Agreement enforceable against the Government?
evidence: Any such clause is unenforceable against the Government.

cases.question: What is the due date for invoice payments under the Prompt Payment clause?
evidence: The 30th day after the designated billing office receives a proper invoice from the Contractor

cases.question: When must invoices for meat or meat food products be paid?
evidence: as close as possible to, but not later than, the 7th day after product delivery

cases.question: What is the payment due date for perishable agricultural commodities?
evidence: the 10th day after product delivery, unless another date is specified in the contract

cases.question: Within how many days will the billing office return an invoice that is not proper?
evidence: the designated billing office will return it within 7 days after receipt

cases.question: What happens when a payment due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday?
evidence: may make payment on the following working day without incurring a late payment interest penalty

cases.question: For computing an interest penalty, when is Government acceptance deemed to occur constructively?
evidence: deemed to occur constructively on the 7th day

cases.question: How soon must the Contractor's written demand for an additional penalty be postmarked?
evidence: postmarked not later than 40 days after the invoice amount is paid

cases.question: Under the Fast Payment Procedure, how quickly are payments made?
evidence: payments will be made within 15 days after the date of receipt of the invoice

cases.question: On what day does the Government consider a payment to have been made?
evidence: considers payment as being made on the day a check is dated or the date of an electronic funds transfer

cases.question: Which regulations does the Government use to compute the interest penalty for late payment?
evidence: compute the interest penalty in accordance with the Office of Management and Budget prompt payment regulations at 5 CFR part 1315

cases.question: What is the deadline for notifying individuals after discovery of a breach of unsecured protected health information?
evidence: in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery of a breach

cases.question: How many residents of a State must a breach involve before prominent media outlets must be notified?
evidence: involving more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction

cases.question: When must breaches involving fewer than 500 individuals be reported to the Secretary?
evidence: not later than 60 days after the end of each calendar year
answers: 60 days after the end of each calendar year

cases.question: For substitute notice to 10 or more individuals, how long must the website posting remain up?
evidence: conspicuous posting for a period of 90 days on the home page

cases.question: How can substitute notice be given when contact information is out of date for fewer than 10 individuals?
evidence: fewer than 10 individuals, then such substitute notice may be provided by an alternative form of written notice, telephone, or other means

cases.question: How long can notification be delayed after an oral statement from a law enforcement official?
evidence: no longer than 30 days from the date of the oral statement

cases.question: When is a breach treated as discovered by a covered entity?
evidence: as of the first day on which such breach is known to the covered entity

cases.question: What must a covered entity demonstrate through a risk assessment to rebut the presumption of a breach?
evidence: demonstrates that there is a low probability that the protected health information has been compromised

cases.question: Breaches occurring on or after what date are covered by the breach notification subpart?
evidence: occurring on or after September 23, 2009

cases.question: Who has the burden of proof that all required breach notifications were made?
evidence: shall have the burden of demonstrating that all notifications were made as required by this subpart

cases.question: By what method must written breach notification be sent to an individual?
evidence: Written notification by first-class mail to the individual at the last known address

cases.question: What is the maximum value of an unsolicited gift an employee may accept per source per occasion?
evidence: aggregate market value of $20 or less per source per occasion

cases.question: What is the calendar-year limit on gifts accepted from one person under the $20 exception?
evidence: does not exceed $50 in a calendar year

cases.question: When someone other than the sponsor pays for free attendance at a widely attended gathering, what is the maximum value of that gift?
evidence: the value of the gift of free attendance does not exceed $480

cases.question: What is the annual limit on informational materials an employee may receive from one person without a written determination?
evidence: informational materials received from any one person does not exceed $100 in a calendar year

cases.question: Above what aggregate value does an award require a written determination by the agency ethics official?
evidence: by the sponsor of the event, exceeds $200

cases.question: When may an employee destroy a tangible gift that cannot be accepted?
evidence: in the case of a tangible item with a market value of $100 or less, the employee may destroy the item

cases.question: What can an employee do with a perishable gift that is impractical to return?
evidence: give the item to an appropriate charity, share the item within the recipient's office, or destroy the item

cases.question: Who counts as a prohibited source under the gift rules?
evidence: Prohibited source means any person who

cases.question: Are coffee and donuts considered a gift?
evidence: Modest items of food and non-alcoholic refreshments, such as soft drinks, coffee, and donuts

cases.question: How is the market value of a gift defined?
evidence: Market value means the cost that a member of the general public would reasonably expect to incur to purchase the gift

cases.question: How must an employee dispose of an intangible gift such as entertainment or a service?
evidence: The employee must promptly reimburse the donor the market value for any entertainment, favor, service, benefit, or other intangible

cases.question: What are the six CSF Core Functions?
evidence: GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER
answers: govern, identify, protect, detect, respond, and recover

cases.question: What are the four CSF Tiers?
evidence: Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), and Adaptive (Tier 4)

cases.question: What is a CSF Community Profile?
evidence: A Community Profile is a baseline of CSF outcomes

cases.question: What does a CSF Target Profile specify?
evidence: A Target Profile specifies the desired outcomes

cases.question: What are Informative References in the CSF?
evidence: Informative References are mappings that indicate relationships between the Core and various standards

cases.question: What was the Cybersecurity Framework called before version 2.0?
evidence: Framework for Improving Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity
answers: framework for improving critical infrastructure cybersecurity

cases.question: What is the publication date of NIST CSWP 29, CSF 2.0?
evidence: February 26, 2024

cases.question: What outcome does the GOVERN Function describe?
evidence: cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored

cases.question: What does CSF subcategory RS.MI-01 state?
evidence: RS.MI-01: Incidents are contained

cases.question: Which email address should suggestions about the CSF be sent to?
evidence: cyberframework@nist.gov

cases.question: What outcome does the DETECT Function describe?
evidence: Possible cybersecurity attacks and compromises are found and analyzed
